result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the diagram right after a short opening and tie it to four numbered steps. Neither recommends writing labels on the diagram itself, since both rely on numbered markers, and A also adds color coding. B frames the page around the path the heat takes and adds useful checks: matching arrow direction to the step order, consistent part names, and alt text. That makes B slightly better. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the diagram first and split the text into four numbered steps that follow the heat. B is better on the rubric: it explicitly asks for one idea per step, says the diagram's labels should be the words the text uses, and on mobile keeps the callout numbers large enough to read. Neither answer says to put labels directly on the diagram next to each part, and B's color-coding adds another key for readers to decode.
